title: Suspended Platform Assembly - Wire Elongation, Vertical Displacement, and Tilt
summary: An assigned two-level rigid-member model linking equilibrium, axial wire extension, signed displacement/tilt, and weighted load-displacement contributions.
courseTopic: Axial deformation, equilibrium of rigid members, displacement compatibility, and small-angle rotation
expectedStudentDeliverable: Physical-system interpretation, student-generated idealization, free-body diagrams, wire-force calculations, elongations, vertical displacement, tilt angles, and a concise engineering assessment.
geometryComplexity: Two-level suspended rigid-body system with four deformable axial wires and eccentric loading.
problemDeliverableType: Annotated free-body diagrams, wire-force calculations, elongations, displacement and tilt calculations, and concise engineering interpretation.
idealizedImageAlt: Instructor free bodies for AB and DC: upward wire tensions on AB, downward applied P, and opposite upper/lower wire forces on DC at the shared node C.
problemStatement:
Suspended platforms transfer supported loads through tensile suspension members to an overhead lifting or supporting system. Their position and orientation can change as those members extend under load. Load location, suspension geometry and axial stiffness can affect both vertical movement and tilt.

Use the industry image to interpret the physical system and develop your own idealization in Q1–Q10. A common, unsolved model and its assigned numerical data will then be supplied for M1–M11 so that the quantitative work uses a shared geometry. The image establishes context; it does not establish the assigned dimensions, material properties or load rating.
engineeringGoal: Estimate load-point displacement and the rotations of the two members in the supplied common model. Explain how each wire contributes to load-point displacement and make an engineering recommendation limited to the assigned first-order model and its assumptions.
commonModelStatement:
For the quantitative phase, use two initially horizontal rigid members DC and AB and four initially vertical axial wires. Fixed ceiling anchors E and F support D and C through wires ED and FC. Wire AH connects point H on DC to lower endpoint A, and wire BC connects C to lower endpoint B. A is vertically below H, and B is vertically below C. The only applied load in this model is the prescribed downward point force P on AB, at distance xP from A.

Use the unsolved geometry, current-input dimensions and Given Data below. The initial geometry must satisfy LDC = xDH + xHC and LAB = xHC, with D–H–C in that order and 0 < xP < LAB. All ten values are instructional assignments. They are not measurements, manufacturer specifications, a validated assembly stiffness or a load rating.

Work from the common assumptions below even if your earlier Q8 model used a different defensible idealization. No quantitative force, extension, displacement or tilt solution is supplied in the student reference geometry.
commonModelAssumptions: The calculation is two-dimensional, quasi-static and first order about the undeformed nodal layout. Out-of-plane and lateral stability are not analyzed.
DC and AB are rigid; their bending, shear and axial deformation are omitted by stipulation, not demonstrated negligible for an actual deck.
E and F have zero displacement. Eye/pin connections transmit the modeled wire forces without externally applied couples. Fixed anchor coordinates do not clamp either rigid member.

All four suspension members are ideal straight, constant-area linear axial wires with the same assigned Aw and Ew. ED and FC have free length Lu; AH and BC have free length Ll. This is an assigned EA model, not a calibrated chain or wire-rope assembly.

Reference lengths and coordinates describe an aligned, unstrained ideal configuration. No initial pretension, seating extension, assembly slack or anchor settlement is included. P is the prescribed load increment from that ideal datum; it is the sole external load in the quantitative model.
The self-weights of both rigid members and all wires are neglected. P is not represented as an experimentally established total weight or an implicit allowance for omitted upper-member weight.

All four wires carry positive tension in the selected configuration. They cannot supply compression or moments. Slack-member, endpoint-load, inclined-wire and alternative active-set models are outside this exercise.

Axial strains and rotations must be small enough for the assigned linear/first-order model. Initial horizontal lever arms and vertical wire directions are used; finite-rotation changes are omitted. The model-status note below states whether quantitative screening limits have been configured.

Displacements v are positive downward. Signed rotations θ are positive clockwise, meaning the right end drops relative to the left. Force equilibrium uses upward-positive forces and counterclockwise-positive moments; these sign conventions serve different equations and are explicitly stated.

Use pound-force: metadata unit lb means lbf here. Use feet for nodal geometry and force moments; convert all lengths to inches for extensions and displacement-slope calculations. Ew is in ksi. Retain unrounded intermediate values.

Material/assembly provenance, proportional-limit evidence, strength, connector behavior, fatigue, dynamics, sag, real deck bending and service limits are not supplied. These results do not establish a real platform's fitness for service.
